slot.brief: Find the range of a rational function like (x²+ax+b)/(quadratic) by setting y = f(x) and imposing discriminant ≥ 0; hard — include a subtle domain exclusion.

working:
Set $N-yD=0$: $(3x-5)\big[(2-5y)x+(1+7y)\big]=0$. The discriminant is $\Delta=(13-4y)^2\geq0$. For $y=\dfrac{2}{5}$, only $x=\dfrac{5}{3}$ solves it; for $y=\dfrac{13}{4}$, the repeated root is $x=\dfrac{5}{3}$. Both are excluded from the domain. Also, $x=\dfrac{7}{5}$ never solves $N-yD=0$; every other $y$ has an allowed solution. Hence the range is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\left\{\dfrac{2}{5},\dfrac{13}{4}\right\}$.

Independent check: Factor and cancel: f(x)=(2x+1)/(5x-7), with x=5/3 and 7/5 excluded. The value 2/5 is never attained; the excluded hole at x=5/3 also removes the value 13/4.
solution:
Factor and cancel: $f(x)=\dfrac{(3x-5)(2x+1)}{(3x-5)(5x-7)}=\dfrac{2x+1}{5x-7}$, with $x\ne\dfrac{5}{3},\dfrac{7}{5}$.
The value $\dfrac{2}{5}$ is never attained, while excluding $x=\dfrac{5}{3}$ also removes $f\!\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)=\dfrac{13}{4}$.
Hence the range is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\left\{\dfrac{2}{5},\dfrac{13}{4}\right\}$.
